strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across 5 datasets and 3 MLLM families demonstrating consistent improvements over training-free baselines and competitive performance with training-based methods (e.g., 75.2 J&F on Ref-DAVIS with Qwen2.5VL, outperforming VISA 69.4 and VideoLISA 68.8)

Clear motivation addressing real limitations of prior work (Loc-Head's poor generalization to reasoning tasks and model-specific visual attention sink heuristics) with a principled training-free alternative

Thoughtful technical design: contrastive fusion directly targets attention sink phenomenon; video-frame fusion leverages complementary properties (temporal context vs. spatial detail); attention consistency score elegantly filters spurious masks
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 4-7) validating each component's contribution, including multi-scale processing, rollout methods, and threshold sensitivity
Good generalizability: method works across diverse MLLMs without model-specific or task-specific modifications, unlike Loc-Head

Well-structured presentation with clear figures (Figs. 1-3) effectively communicating the approach
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contributions are relatively incremental—contrastive fusion is simple subtraction (alternatives unexplored), video-frame fusion is simple averaging (no learnable combination tested), attention rollout is established prior work

Background prompt design depends on fragile object category extraction: if MLLM fails to identify category correctly, background prompt generation fails; no error analysis or alternative strategies provided

Fundamental unresolved limitations with sparse/thin object attention: large objects with sparse attention trigger false negatives via s^ac (Fig. 10a), thin structures not captured (Fig. 10b), briefly-visible small objects problematic (Fig. 10c)—these are common scenarios, not edge cases

Missing computational cost analysis: requires multiple MLLM forward passes (object/background prompts, category choice, video/frame-level processing) plus SAM2 overhead; no runtime comparison with baselines—critical for practical deployment

No error bars or statistical significance testing (single runs reported); fixed 16-frame sampling with no sensitivity analysis; prompt design not ablated; missing metrics for temporal consistency and per-class performance
